kill_chain_signals.contact: fraudsters contact via online dating sites, social media platforms, text messages, or compromise existing friend/family accounts on Facebook
kill_chain_signals.pretext: perpetrators claim to be successful cryptocurrency investors, create fake celebrity endorsements with deepfakes, or pose as friends/family in distress
kill_chain_signals.payment: victims persuaded to invest in cryptocurrency with promise of high returns, open and fund new crypto accounts, or pay extortion demands
kill_chain_signals.movement: fraudsters direct victims to transfer crypto investment to alternate crypto addresses they control
kill_chain_signals.cashout: once cryptocurrency transaction is completed, it is unlikely to be reversed

red_flags: Someone you haven't met in person professes their love to you
A suspect that tries to move communication to a more private or different method of communication (Whatsapp, Signal or Discord, etc.)
Any attempts to meet in person get cancelled or there's always an excuse to not meet up
Investment opportunities with higher than normal returns
Requests for remote access to your device in order to teach you how to invest
key_quote: Fraudsters are increasingly compromising profiles on social platforms like Facebook.
title: Social media fraud
